D30·v8ec — 2026-10-10
chose: 2.6 tiered verify is opt-in through `--verify-quick <cmd>` (recorded as run_started.verify_quick, needs --verify; a resume keeps its own). A task with no verify of its own is gated on it, `{files}` = the paths the task touched, holds uncommitted or committed since its launch (since the run base on lanes), single-quoted; at the touched-list cap it runs --verify. --verify runs once when every task of a phase is resolved and one is in the window (tasks whose latest own pass came after the last --verify pass), and at the closing sweep; a pass on the exact tree covers the quick-tier checks there. A failure is bisected over the window's task commits (HEAD of each task's latest pass when the tree was clean), each probe in a clean lane recorded against the task whose commit it ran on, and the task owning the first failing commit is reopened. A serial tiered run claims one lane from the pool for the bisect, the first time it needs one.
over: Deriving the quick tier from a built-in runner table (session-driver D8); recording the full gate once per window task; bisecting in the operator's checkout, or in a fresh worktree per probe; a phase-end gate built into runTask, where a lanes run cannot see which lanes are busy
because: The operator states both commands, so no runner table is guessed. One record per execution, against the task whose tree it checked, keeps the fold's per-task attempt counting honest. A serial run's checkout is shared with peers (M5), so a probe can only run in its own worktree; the lane pool already gives one with dependencies installed once. That is an exception to session-driver D6 for tiered runs only: without --verify-quick, --lanes 1 stays byte-identical. The coordinator's loop knows held tasks and busy lanes, and inside the merge queue no landing moves the base under the gate.
